description: The bar chart, titled "QLoRA," compares the computational cost measured in FLOPs across different fine-tuning methods for language models. The vertical axis, labeled "# FLOPs," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from $10^{18}$ to $10^{20}$, while the horizontal axis lists six methods: Full FT, TAG, LoRA, MTL-FT, QLoRA, and Ours. The bars for Full FT, TAG, LoRA, MTL-FT, and QLoRA are all orange and decrease in height from left to right, indicating a reduction in FLOPs. The bar for "Ours" is green and is the shortest, visually representing the lowest computational cost among the methods. Specifically, the "Ours" method requires approximately $5 \times 10^{18}$ FLOPs, which is about 45% less than the "Full FT" method, which requires around $9 \times 10^{18}$ FLOPs. This visual evidence supports the claim in the caption that the proposed method achieves high performance with significantly lower computational cost.
